scope: FF9SpecialEffectPlugin GTE RTPS/RTPT: MAC0 and IR0 (GteRtps.cs)
original_pc: MAC0 = DQB + q * (low 32 bits of the address of the DQA register), so the result depends on where Windows loads the DLL; the harness saw it relocated to 0x7ff880a20000
memoria_reference: The same formula over the address of Memoria's own ModuleData copy, which gives another value again
tantalus_default: The address at the DLL's preferred base, 0x80211FAC, every run
evidence: crates/tantalus-sfx/tests/oracle.rs gte_matches_the_dll: the port matches the DLL exactly when given the DLL's load address
rationale: The original value changes from launch to launch; a fixed value keeps effects and replays deterministic. It feeds MAC0 and IR0 (the depth-cue factor) only

scope: FF9SpecialEffectPlugin StartPsxTask (sub_180048B10): the entry block flags
original_pc: The DLL zeroes only the first 8 bytes of the 24-byte request and passes the dword at +0x14 to PsxInitEntryBlock; task scripts store it there (Thunder ef003 stores its update function 0x801E7CEC)
memoria_reference: The rewrite treats the request as 16 bytes, zeroes +8 and +12 and passes +12, which no script writes, so the flags are always 0 and Thunder faults in frame 64
tantalus_default: The DLL: read +0x14 (cs2rs Patches); the rest of the request starts zeroed where the DLL leaves stack contents
evidence: crates/tantalus-sfx/tests/plugin.rs sweep: effects 3 4 5 24 38 and others match the DLL only with the patch
rationale: Vanilla behavior; the rewrite's version is a rewrite error and breaks the effect

scope: FF9SpecialEffectPlugin port: host addresses of heap blocks and the native stack
original_pc: Windows heap and stack addresses, different every launch
memoria_reference: Managed and native addresses of the Unity process
tantalus_default: Heap blocks from 0x2_0000_0000, each on its own 4 MB boundary and never reused; a 4 MB stack under 0x40_0040_0000 that grows down
evidence: crates/tantalus-sfx/tests/plugin.rs probe_lockstep: module data and the PSX address mapper windows match the DLL frame by frame
rationale: Effects only see these addresses through the PSX address mapper, which opens one 3 MB window per distant block; fixed far-apart addresses open the same windows as the DLL and keep runs deterministic
